title: Saudi-led coalition says new attack at Riyadh airport causes fire, day after strike kills 12
gist: Reuters via Al-Monitor: a new projectile hit Terminal 4 of Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on Oct 11, a day after a Houthi strike killed 12 and wounded 300+, the deadliest on Saudi Arabia in over a decade. The Houthis warned airlines off all Saudi airports except Mecca and Medina, Trump said the US was weighing joining Saudi strikes, and Riyadh kept a major energy conference running.

insights.claim: An attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport on Saturday Oct 10, 2026 killed 12 people and wounded more than 300, the deadliest such strike on Saudi Arabia in over a decade.
insights.so_what: Marks a step-change in the Houthis' ability to inflict mass casualties in the Saudi capital, raising Gulf country risk.
insights.quote: The airport remains closed after an attack there on Saturday killed 12 people and wounded more than 300 others, the deadliest such strike on the kingdom in over a decade

insights.speaker: Al-Monitor

insights.claim: The Saudi-led coalition said a further 'unidentified projectile' hit Terminal 4 of Riyadh's international airport on Sunday Oct 11, causing a fire, while Saudi air defences intercepted a cruise missile near the airport.
insights.so_what: Repeated hits despite air defences show Saudi interception is not airtight against Houthi cruise missiles.
insights.quote: The coalition also said Saudi air defences had intercepted a cruise missile in the vicinity of King Khalid International Airport.

insights.speaker: Al-Monitor

insights.claim: The Saturday strike was the third attack on Riyadh's airport within a week; the two earlier attacks killed four people and one heavily damaged a parked Saudi commercial plane.
insights.so_what: A sustained, escalating tempo of strikes rather than a one-off suggests prolonged disruption to Saudi aviation.
insights.quote: Four people were killed in the two previous attacks on the airport earlier in the week.

insights.claim: The Houthis publicly warned all airlines, workers and travellers to avoid Saudi airports and airspace, declaring them a theatre of operations, with the exception of the airports in Mecca and Medina.
insights.so_what: Explicit threats to civil aviation can push carriers and insurers to reroute or suspend Saudi flights, hitting tourism and Vision 2030-style business travel.
insights.quote: We renew our warning to all airlines, experts, employees, workers and travellers against using Saudi airports and airspace, as they are vulnerable to attack

insights.claim: The Houthis sought to shift blame for collateral damage onto Riyadh, saying Saudi Arabia bears responsibility for any failed interceptions.
insights.so_what: Signals the group expects debris and failed interceptions and is preparing narrative cover for civilian casualties.

themes.theme: Yemen war escalation and US involvement

insights.claim: Saudi Arabia escalated its military role in Yemen in recent weeks, launching strikes on the Houthis and backing a Yemeni government counteroffensive after the Houthis seized strategic Red Sea coast territory the previous month.
insights.so_what: Houthi control of more Red Sea coastline raises shipping-lane risk and explains Riyadh's escalation.

insights.claim: The Houthi-run foreign ministry warned that further Saudi military action in Yemen would bring a stronger, reciprocal response and that 'worse is yet to come'.
insights.so_what: Points to a tit-for-tat escalation spiral rather than de-escalation in the near term.

insights.claim: President Donald Trump said the United States was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis, a conflict described as a spillover from the wider war on Iran that the US and Israel launched in February 2026.
insights.so_what: Direct US entry would widen the regional war and add to oil and shipping risk premia.

insights.claim: Despite the airport closure, the Saudi Energy Ministry kept a five-day WPC Energy Congress going in Riyadh about 10 km from the airport, with state TV citing over 70 ministers, 300 company executives and 25+ international energy organisations confirmed.
insights.so_what: Riyadh is prioritising a business-as-usual signal to the energy industry, though in-person attendance was unclear.
insights.quote: State TV said more than 70 ministers, 300 company executives and representatives of over 25 international energy organisations had confirmed their attendance.
insights.locator: INTERNATIONAL ENERGY CONFERENCE STILL GOING AHEAD
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor

insights.claim: A ministerial meeting of the International Energy Forum was also set to proceed in Riyadh, with its plenary held behind closed doors.
insights.so_what: Key producer-consumer energy dialogue continues under security pressure, with reduced transparency.

insights.claim: Saudi authorities suspended in-person classes and moved all students, teachers and staff to remote learning from Sunday to Thursday after the airport attacks.
insights.so_what: Shows the security threat is disrupting daily civilian life in Riyadh, not just aviation.
